value.body: A BBA track focused on managing money in a business — financial accounting, corporate finance, financial markets, investment and portfolio basics, banking, and cost accounting, within a broader management degree.

items.label: Regulator
items.note: Alongside the affiliating university; BBA, BCA and BMS were brought under AICTE from 2024-25

items.label: Demat accounts in India
items.note: A measure of retail market participation, not of jobs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in any stream. Admission is by Class 12 marks, CUET-UG, or a university's own test. Most students pick the specialisation in the second or third year; some institutes admit directly to a named programme.

value.title: At a glance
items: It has fewer accounting papers than a B.Com and more management subjects.
Several market-facing roles need SEBI-mandated NISM certifications, such as mutual fund distribution.
Entry roles include financial analyst trainee, credit or loan processing, banking sales and fund operations.
Common next steps: an MBA (Finance), CFA or FRM, or bank recruitment exams.
